drug_class: NSAID (pain reliever/anti-inflammatory) combined with Antihistamine (sleep aid)
purpose: This medication is used to help relieve minor aches and pains while also helping you fall asleep. It is great for nighttime use when pain like headaches, backaches, or muscle soreness is making it hard to sleep. It is not meant for daytime use since it will make you feel drowsy.
how_it_works: The ibuprofen part works by blocking certain chemicals in your body that cause pain, swelling, and fever. The diphenhydramine part is an antihistamine that causes drowsiness, which helps you fall asleep faster. Together, they tackle your pain and help your body rest at the same time.
common_side_effects: Drowsiness or grogginess the next morning, dry mouth, upset stomach, dizziness, constipation, and blurry vision. You may also feel a little groggy or foggy when you wake up, so avoid driving until you feel fully alert.
warnings: Do not take this with alcohol, other sleep aids, or other medications containing ibuprofen or diphenhydramine. Avoid if you have kidney problems, stomach ulcers, heart disease, or glaucoma. Do not give to children under 12. Do not use for more than 2 weeks without talking to your doctor. Older adults should be especially careful as drowsiness increases fall risk.
typical_dosing: The typical adult dose is 2 tablets (each containing 200mg ibuprofen and 25mg diphenhydramine) taken at bedtime. Only take it once per night and do not take more than 2 tablets in 24 hours. Always take with a full glass of water and a light snack to avoid stomach upset.
